utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Having -- I beg your pardon, I withdraw that. Do you see that map in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see it before me now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are those red markings, were those red markings made by you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I made them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do they indicate the locations through which your unit advanced its attack from 4th to 8th August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I tender this map in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may, Ms. Mahindartne, but apart from a few dots on the map, are we going to receive information as to from where he moved --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to where?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's -- of course, it's already in the 92 ter statement. If you wish I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That suggests that I could read the names on this map and I know that I'm old and you have got glasses, but that's really impossible on the basis of this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I will -- for the record I will get him to identify the places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you say I see some in the south, for example, I see four in the southern area, then I see one a little bit higher up a bit to the east and then further up north-east at a bit more distance I see another dot and then I see north of that another one. If the movement was from south-west to north, a bit north-east, further north, and then a little bit north, if that is the -- if that is it, then fine. If it is different, I'd like to know. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is actually going to the subject of dispute, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It actually should be more precise than the dots on the map. He should be taken through specifically where he says or claims that he went through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I could do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it up to you, but for the Chamber, I mean we've got a map with a few dots. It is as if you get something from your grandchildren and you put it on the wall. I mean it's -- for me at this moment it has a similar meaning, although I know it is the Krajina area. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, if you could look at your statement, paragraph 6 you say -- paragraph 6, it is the same paragraph number in the B/C/S version. You refer to starting your axis of attack for Operation Oluja on 4th August from Pavasovici, which is near Skradin. Now, could you identify as to what that first dot, that is the dot at the most south -- southern point of the map, the first dot is.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's our point of departure. Pavasovici village near the place called Skradin, not Skradun. So it is Pavasovici village near Skradin.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, there are two dots close to each other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the map on the screen rather than the text because the text is easier to read so that we can zoom in on ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On the first, for the record the first dot indicates the place Skradin. Now, the dot just above it, you have written a name in ink. Could you identify that for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Pavasovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, was that the point at which you started your axis of attack on 4th August?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I again ask to have the -- the map also in English, because in English in the e-court system we still have the text of the statement, and I cannot manipulate anything unless -- could we have therefore the map in both versions, English ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still the text. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't understand. You wanted the map in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have two versions of what is shown and now it is in the English version as well, it is the map, because if the map is there we can zoom in and zoom out ourselves and not dependant on what is done by the registry. It is fine now. So, therefore, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 6 itself, you mention that the axis of attack started from Pavasovici towards Sonkovici. Could you indicate where Sonkovici is. Is that the third dot?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Perhaps on e-court if you could take the cursor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness could use the cursor, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is Sonkovici. And you -- how long did you remain in Sonkovici?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: A short time. We were moving rather fast. But, as I said in my statement, to be more precise the first day we attempted an attack on Sonkovici and that detained us, so the breakout through Sonkovici succeeded only the next day. So that is the time we spent at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, from Sonkovici, where did your unit move on to? And if I could assist you, you have mentioned that in paragraph 8 of your statement, you mentioned that you moved on to Djevrska. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We moved in the direction of Djevrska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're on the map, for reasons that will you see in cross-examination, just if we could get an understanding of what the map is intended to show. If it is intended to show places where the witnesses claims to have been, I accept the map. If it is going to the route that he took, then I would ask that the dots be connected so that we see what route the witness claims his unit took through these various places. I think there's a distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindartne --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's the places, Mr. President. It's not been moved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we -- if you move from one spot to another, we do not know yet and we're not asking you at this moment how you went from the one spot to the other. Just whether you -- whether that was one of your next stops. Okay, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you identify where -- what the third -- Djevrska can you just move the cursor to Djevrska?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I think I don't see it, Djevrska, on the map. I only see another point.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's further up than that, if you could move the map further up.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, now it's in --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Padjene.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: To the right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're right. Djevrska is here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And from Djevrska, where did you move to, your next stop?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is that where you've -- okay. The name Kistanje is indicated in that red spot, for the record. Could you please move the map up. Can you place your cursor at the next red spot.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What is that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I see I marked Padjene, but right now I cannot see this mark on the map. It's too small now. It should be Padjene.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can we move the map further up, please. Could you place your cursor at the next red spot.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Zrmanja.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And can we move the map further up. And a little to the -- yes. Could you place your cursor at the next red spot. What is that position?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Donji Srb, or Lower Srb.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in your statement you describe at which point and at which -- during which time-frame your unit moved through these locations. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for point of clarification again, I think it is going be unclear from his statements, she says which -- his unit. If we could have a definition of that, given that in his statement which is now in evidence he claims at various points that he got separated from his unit, that he was off with volunteers, et cetera, so...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me rephrase, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In your statement, you describe as to at what time, when and how you moved through these locations, you, along with the other personnel who were moving with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at the proofing meeting, when you examined the map, you made a certain correction with regard to the time-frame.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The answer I just gave takes into account the corrections to my prior statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me take to you paragraph 13 of your 1995 statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I believe it is 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: October 2004/January 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Mr. President. 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There you mentioned that you entered Kistanje on 6th August. Is that correct? You say: "I think it was the same day of 6th August, 1995, our same group of seven volunteers went through Kistanje."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: May I again get -- could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in paragraph 13 of your 2005 statement, you refer to going through Kistanje on 6th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In paragraph 14 of the same statement, you would say that on the same day, you moved to Padjene.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said then that I went to Padjene on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to that, you made a correction, which is at paragraph 4 of the proofing note. It is referred to paragraph 4, 5, and 6.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could the court usher please help me locate those paragraphs? I can't find them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindartne, why not put to the witness what his correction was, the correction being that most likely on the 6th that he returned from -- to Sibenik and then moved on --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, that's what we're talking about, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, wasn't it the case that you informed the Office of the Prosecutor that you had to make a correction with regard to your time-frame; that is, that after entering Kistanje on 6th of August, from there, you returned to Sibenik, to spend the night of 6th August in Sibenik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindartne, you have presented it as a fact when the witness in his additional statement said that he believes it was on the 6th and therefore that he concluded that it was on the night of the 6th --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- [Overlapping speakers] ... in Sibenik, but let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You want to say that you recall leaving Sibenik in a bus to Padjene and you believe that was on 7th August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Subject to that correction, when do you believe you were in Padjene?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 7th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And where did you spend the night of 7th August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Padjene, the night of the 7th on to the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And on 8th, where did you move on to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To Donji Srb.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you reached Donji Srb on the 8th, was it already in the hands of the Croatian forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on to another area, Mr. President, do you wish me to go through the route? I did not consider --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It -- I leave it entirely in your hands. What you did is you presented the map to us with a lot of dots on it without any clue as to a sequence. The sequence is now there, no details about route is there at this very moment apart than that at a certain moment the witness returned to Sibenik and then so that the sequence is now more or less clear, but what roads they took I don't know what the relevance would be so therefore I leave it entirely to you, but there seems to be a matter of dispute, so I don't know yet what the dispute is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the entire reason for presenting the map is as a demonstrative tool, and the relevance is the locations because the witness speaks with regard to the locations, and the sequence is provided in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is good enough for you to deal with apparently what will be a dispute, then I leave it in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, may I take you to paragraph 8 of your statement. Mr. Gojanovic, if you could just look at paragraph 8 of your statement. And I'm referring to statement P194. You refer to being involved in mop-up operations and searching the area.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, what exactly did you do in mop-up operations? Did you enter civilian houses?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We entered all the houses and buildings that were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you entered the houses, were they occupied or were they empty?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, all the houses were empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when you went into these empty houses, did you see any evidence as to the circumstances under which the occupants had left?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you saw?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Some houses were completely closed, and there was no one in them. Other houses were open, and we even found sometimes on the tables a warm meal half-eaten, which pointed to me that these people had fled -- left their homes immediately before we arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in the course of these mop-up operations, what did you do when you met civilians?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian would be taken out onto the road and would be made to lie down on the ground, and then that person would be searched to find out if there were any concealed weapons. And then the other part of the military unit would search that building, or the house where the civilians were, in order to discover any enemies, if they were there, or some hidden weapons or some other danger. Then the civilians would be put under guard until the military component arrived, the military component that was in charge of gathering these civilians and then transporting them to the centre where all civilians were supposed to be taken and kept under military supervision.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know why the civilians were kept under military supervision?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that they were under military supervision.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you referred to transporting the civilians to the centre. Are you referring to collection centres?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindartne, I would like to hear an answer to that previous question. Why were civilians treated as you described? You said they were kept under military supervision and taken to centres. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I provided the explanation in my statement in very simple terms. In a military operation, it is never certain who is a civilian and who is a disguised soldier, and in that sense we also had to take into account and to make sure that the soldiers, the troops who were advancing on the territory were secure so that all these civilians that we encountered would be transported to these collection centres. And just let me add, I don't know who was in charge of the collection centres, because I didn't have occasion to see it for myself, but I know that the transport of civilians to these centre -- to the collection centre was organised by the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you under instructions to deal with what you called "civilians" this way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were issued brief instructions relating to the civilian population, to the effect that their security should be ensured and that casualties should be prevented in the course of the military operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that is a different matter. You're certainly aware of that. You earlier said that the concern was you never know whether the civilians were real civilians and not soldiers in disguise. That's quite a different reason than saying that -- that their security should be ensured, because I take it that the security of soldiers in disguise was not your concern at that moment. At least that is not what you explained to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just point out what you admonished me yesterday about monocausal. I'm not sure if there could be two reasons that he's giving for that treatment of civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but in the one case he considers the persons involved to be potentially soldiers in disguise and so we are dealing with two different approaches. But, okay, it is no problem that you remind me of what I said yesterday. Please proceed. But ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you would like me to answer how we concluded that a person was a civilian and that another person was a soldier in disguise? If I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that is at least a question that came into my mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] yes. [Interpretation] It is hard, in the field, to actually tell who is a civilian and who is a soldier in disguise. But the suspicion alone is not enough to treat a person as a -- as an enemy, a confirmed enemy. In keeping with that, all civilians were transported and the transport was organised by the military, to the collection centres and as far as I'm concerned as a soldier, I no longer had the concern whether this was a civilian or a soldier in disguise once I handed over these -- these persons to the military organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now you're talking about civilians in a rather general way. Would that include women, elderly, youngsters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, not the smallest children, but this absolutely encompasses all individuals, as far as the suspicion was concerned as to a possible threat from them. That's -- in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you consider women, if you had found no weapons on them when you searched them, did you consider them to be a potential threat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that you only transported or only referred women with weapons to the units that transported them into the collection centres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. All civilians were transported to these collection centres. In other words, once it was established that an individual was a civilian, this individual was transported to the collection centre. As far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, on that following the question from the Bench, if I take to you paragraph 10 of your statement, Mr. Gojanovic, you -- the bottom part of that paragraph, you refer to finding a group of three to four people, civilians, whom you say included an old man who lied about weapons as he was hiding a machine-gun in a box of corn. And you go on to say: "Because they had lied about the existence of weapons, we took those people from the house so they could be taken to a collection centre." Now, why were they sent to a collection centre? Was there an expectation of interrogation that was to take place in the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I object to the leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I hadn't finished the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but the leading element of the question was already there, Ms. Mahindartne, unless you would like to ask later what kind of food they got, but that apparently was not the case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I apologise. I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What was expected to happen to those civilians at the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They were expected to be registered, each civilian who was in the area and taken to the collection centre and, on the other hand, to examine all the circumstances of that civilian relative to the potential enemy forces which -- with which they might have been in contact. In keeping with that, I would like to add that it was just one element of our caution, because we found this weapon hidden in a box of corn, thus by -- thus, we removed the threat from that to other Croatian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And where was this examination of all circumstances? Was it -- where was it expected to take place? At the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Although this was not my task and it was not something that I had to have knowledge about, but I assumed that this was to be done in the collection centre. However, as a soldier who had to travel long distances, I was practically no longer preoccupied with this issue, I was more preoccupied with what I had to encounter on my way along the axis of our action.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you know as to who manned those collection centres, who carried out those tasks relating to examination of circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on to another area, Mr. Gojanovic, if I could take you to -- take you back to paragraph 9. You refer to -- you describe an incident where a member of the 113th Brigade killed, shot dead, one of two SVK soldiers had just surrendered and where you had to intervene to prevent the killing of the other, and this was on 6th August 1995. Now, prior to setting off on the operation on 4th August, were instructions given to you or were you aware of instructions being given as to how you were supposed to treat prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindartne, in your previous question you left it open that one or two soldiers were killed, whereas in paragraph 9 I find that one soldier out of two arrested was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I mentioned one of two, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I think it is -- yes. No. I understood one or two and I see that on the transcript it says one of two.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's what I said, Mr. President, one of two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of such instructions being issued to members -- I'm sorry. You already answered that. In paragraph 4, if I could take you back on your statement. In paragraph 4 you referred to your mobilisation on 2nd August, and in fact you referred to a huge mass of people arriving in Jadrija, pardon me pronunciation, on 2nd August for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, from 2nd to 4th, until you set off on the attack, where were you and this large group of people based at?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We were based in buildings in the place Jadrija.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, during that period, were any instructions given as to how to treat civilians or civilian property?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. He has already answered that question and said that he was given instructions on how to treat civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I'm just asking about the period 2nd August to 4th. I will get to the part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, different period of time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: During that period were instructions given as to how the units were to treat civilians or civilian property or prisoners of war at the time you were waiting to go on attack from 2nd August to 4th August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't get any.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, previously, I think in response to a question from the Bench, you -- in describing how civilians were treated in the course of mop-up operations, you said that instructions had been given to ensure their security.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I said that we got some guide-lines as to how to treat civilians but this was during the action. However, at the very beginning of the action or during the preparations for it, we didn't get any instruction. And if I can add, in the two days that we were in Jadrija we practically had no idea whether this was Operation Storm or some other kind of action or operation or some other kind of preparations.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now to clarify that, when did you receive those instructions as to how to deal with the civilians? And I'm referring to the issue you spoke of earlier on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the operation, but not directly from my commander, because, as I mentioned to the Prosecution, my situation was a bit more specific. It didn't quite fit the military order. So, in other words, we got it -- I got it during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You got it from whom?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the soldiers who were with me with whom I was in contact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what were those instructions? Were the instructions -- or how exactly was that information conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was conveyed, if I may say so, en passant. So they said, Search the buildings seek any civilians and discover potential enemies, so that was done in the course of the operation, not before it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, one last question on that. In the course of the operation did you or any of the units receive formal instructions from your command as to how to treat civilians or --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object again at least to the -- at least until there's some foundation established as to what "formal" means.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's just that I believe the witness's evidence on this issue is not clear and I thought it would be of interest to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that Mr. Misetic thinks that the clarification you are seeking remains still a bit in the dark. If you do not deal with the -- what is formal. So if you please address that as well in your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you receive any orders, did you or the soldiers around you receive any orders from your command, as to how to deal with civilians or civilian property or prisoners of war during the course of the operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I'm going to object to the extent that she's asked now for the soldiers the around him. If she wants to ask him personally, that is one thing, but I would ask for foundation, then, as to how this witness is going to testify about other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will withdraw the reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are other soldiers. Please reformulate in your question so that we have -- apart from that of course, if you're talking about orders given, I can hear orders that are given to people standing next to me. That's -- so therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But there light of the prior testimony where he's saying he heard it from other soldiers, you know, I don't know how --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But, Ms. Mahindartne, please formulate the question in such a way that there's no reason whatsoever for Mr. Misetic to object and then we'll hear the answer, because that is what we're hear for, to hear your answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you ever issued any orders as to how to treat civilians, civilian property or prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any other persons around you being given such orders?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In my platoon, while we were in Jadrija, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At any stage were you informed by any of your colleagues, your fellow soldiers that they had received such orders?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the operation, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In the course of the operation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of operation this was just in casual conversation that really wasn't anything like an order. It was just our discussion as to how to act in such situations and our agreement in the field itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question was were you ever informed by a soldier, a fellow soldier or fellow officer, a fellow soldier that they had received orders that they were to treat civilians and civilian property in such-and-such a manner?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in that same -- in the paragraph 9 that we just referred to, with regard to the killing of the prisoner of war, did you see what -- as to what was done with the body?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you later at least hear as to what was done? Did you learn about it later on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see the body the next day, for instance, or later on in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never saw it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: While we were still on paragraph for one more question on that, taking you back to paragraph 4, referring to the other people who were mobilised with you on the 2nd of August you say that some people were clearly unsuitable for a serious operation like Oluja. Now did you --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you ever find out in the course of the two-day stay as if there were any persons amongst that group who were from -- who were former residents of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on to another area, if I take you to paragraph 10, you refer to an incident where you intervened and stopped soldiers attempting to go set fire to a house with an elderly woman.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, how did you know that there was a woman inside the house? Because in your 2008 statement you explained that you did not know if those soldiers were trying to burn the house, whether they knew there was a woman or not, you did not know. It is stated in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could, Your Honour, have the witness look at a direct reference to the 2008 statement so that we all know exactly what his version of events is with respect to that incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I can take you also to paragraph 5 of the 2008 statement, if you look at the 2008 statement, paragraph 5. I'm referring to, for the record, P195. There you explain that you did not know if in fact the soldiers themselves knew if there was an elderly woman inside the house. That's a correction you made.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Just a minute. [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I'm saying. They didn't know that the elderly woman was inside.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So how did you know that there was a woman inside the house?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because I had seen her previously in that house. She was extremely thin and old, and there was no need to treat her in the way I mentioned previously when I talked about our discussions how to treat civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So before this incident, it pre-supposes that you went into that house.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Why did you go into that house?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It was one of the houses that I searched, and we shouldn't forget that the seven of us had spent an entire night in Djevrska and it was our duty to search and check as many buildings as we could. First of all, for our own safety, and, in the second place, it was our duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what made you go back to that house?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Croatian soldiers entered Djevrska early that morning, and I thought I would go and see what was going on with that woman.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What was reason for you to take that step, because Croatian soldiers had entered the -- entered Djevrska.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object again to the leading. The question was fine, what was the reason for you to take that step. The next part of the question is unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Well, I don't see -- because Croatian soldiers had entered. Mr. President, I just --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He did not say that he -- again, I don't want to testify in front of the witness. He did not say what she's saying at the end. He said he went down there. Then he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And apparently, although you had not finished your sentence yet, but if you say what was the reason, you're asking for a why, and if you then continue with because, it's not under all circumstances that such a second part of a sentence would be leading, but I do understand Mr. Misetic quite well that he fears that leading was to be expected.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, let me ask the question again. I will rephrase it. What was the reason for you to go back?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The reason I went there was that Croatian soldiers had entered that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: How did you see Croatian soldiers entering the house?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Because they were very close to me when they entered.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I went inside and looked around.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what did you see?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I saw that the soldiers started to set the bed on fire without even noticing the old woman hiding in the corner of the room. So I told them she was there, I drew their attention to her, and took her outside.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you ask the Croatian soldiers as to why they were setting the bed on fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that sort of detail anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you aware as to why they were setting the bed on fire?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is the same question asked twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President, I will withdrew that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Let me take you, moving on, let me take to you paragraph 11 of your statement, where you say that you left Djevrska, that when you left it, it was okay, but when you returned about a week later, it was completely destroyed. I'm sorry, it is paragraph 12, it's not 11: "When we left the town of Djevrska it was okay, but when I returned about a week later it had been completely destroyed. Now, you testified earlier that you left Djevrska on 6th August and moved into Kistanje. Is that the time that you mention when you say you left -- when you left Djevrska, it was okay. Was that the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now when you say "okay," what exactly do you mean? Was there anything that you observed in Djevrska, in terms of damage, destruction at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Some houses were burned down, damaged, looted. There had been a lot of arson, looting --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question was at the time that you left on the 6th you say it was okay. Yes. At that time, what was the state of Djevrska?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I hadn't understood. At the time the whole place was mainly intact. There was no observable damage. I think it was completely intact, even.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And then when you return a week later, what was the nature of the destruction you observed? Could you give any insight?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then, at that time, I noticed quite a large number of torched houses, destroyed houses, burglarised, devastated, looted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 9 of your statement, for the record P194, you mentioned that when you left Djevrska on the 6th, the 113th Brigade formally entered Djevrska at 7.15 in the morning. This is on the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when your unit moved to your -- your little group moved from Djevrska to Kistanje, did the rest of the units of the 113th Brigade also move with you, leave Djevrska with you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that all the units of the 113th left Djevrska at the time and accompanied me to Kistanje, because I simply couldn't see far enough behind me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you know if any units remained in Djevrska from 6th August up until the time you returned a week later?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Moving on, taking to you paragraph 13 of P194, you mentioned that when your unit moved on to Kistanje you saw some soldiers who were checking houses but that others were also looting and burning some houses.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's what I said, that some troops were already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And later on, in fact, you described the goods that were being looted as televisions and other goods you say that soldiers had no need for.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, did you see soldiers taking these items out of the houses?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Today, after so much time, I can say with certainty that there was looting, but I cannot summon a single particular image of a soldier carrying out a television set.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in the same statement you refer to soldiers burning houses. Do you recall seeing soldiers setting houses on fire?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Kistanje, I cannot recall seeing somebody setting a house on fire, but what I saw was that houses were either burning or burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did you see anybody in the vicinity of these burning houses when you entered Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. A lot of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What were they doing? Were they just standing around, or what was going on?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You could say that it was rather chaotic. Soldiers were moving from house to house, and all in all, there was no order to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in that same paragraph you say: "Some soldiers were checking the houses but some others were also looting and burning some houses." Now, what exactly led to you conclude that those burning houses were -- you know, that the burning done by the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From what I saw at the time, I inferred and had a certain impression of the situation. However, today I can no longer summon from my memory a single example that would explain to you how I make that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, at the time - this is 6th August - were there civilians present in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you see any civilians present in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that question was just asked twice again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that is a different question, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether there were any civilians. The witness said I do not know. That means that there may have been civilians which he might not have observed, and then the next question was whether he observed any civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If he saw civilians, then they would be present in Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, it is a different question and the question should have been put in the reverse order. That, I would agree with you, yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I repeat that question to you, Mr. Gojanovic. Did you see any civilians in Kistanje on 6th August.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember any civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: At this time do you know as to who had control of this area? In terms of when I say "who," I'm not asking for an individual but which force. The civilian police or the military? Who had control of this area?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The military.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, do you know as to the units present in this area, and when I say "the area," I'm referring to the area you travelled through from 4th to 8th August. Do you know as to which Military District those units belonged to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again if we could have some foundation which units are we talking about before asking about the Military District. What units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my question is as to whether the military units present there belonged to a particular Military District or not, whether he is able to answer that question, and I don't think it is necessary to identify the units present because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could do that step by step, that is, did you see any military operation in what appeared to be units, do you have any further information about these units, and then do you know to whom these units -- if the answer until then will be in the affirmative, then to ask whether the witness knows anything about the hierarchy, to whom was this unit, if there were units, subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. I will approach it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Gojanovic, can I take you to paragraph 13 of your statement. I think you have it right before you. And you say that when you entered Kistanje on 6th August 1995 with your own platoon, the Croatian military was present and you say that the 4th Guards Brigade had already been through the town. Now you yourself, have served in the 4th Guards Brigade. Do you know to which Military District the 4th Guards Brigade belonged?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge it belonged to the Military District in Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now further down you say that at the time you saw the burning in Kistanje, there were units belonging to the Zadar Brigade present in Kistanje. Do you know to which Military District the Zadar Brigade belonged?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sorry to keep interrupting, Your Honour, but the Zadar Brigade is not a -- I mean, if there can be more precision as to what the witness refers to when he refers to that brigade, that is not a formation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- can do it in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, this is what the witness testified and Ms. Ms. Mahindartne is perfectly entitled to ask further questions in -- as follow-up to this answer. Please proceed. Yes. Could you please answer that question whether you know to which Military District the Zadar Brigade was subordinate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say with certainty whether it would be the district of Zadar or Split, but it was Zadar Brigade indubitably.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What about your brigade, the 113th Sibenik Brigade, to which Military District did it belong?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe a Military District is a rather broad affair, and I believe it belonged to the Military District in Split as a centre. In terms of military configuration. But in -- in my mind the Sibenik Brigade was always Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 13 itself, you estimate that on 6th August there was something like 35 to 40 per cent of houses which are burning. Did you come, arrive at that estimate based on your observations in Kistanje on 6th August itself or during a period of time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During my passage, I got to the conclusion that a large number of houses had been burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And when you say your passage, and I'm referring to Kistanje, was it on 6th August, this estimate was arrived at based on your observations on 6th August, or are you referring to a period of time? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR GOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said you saw soldiers checking houses, some looting, some burning. Now were these individual soldiers just coming into the area or were they structured units present in the area?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again I have to rise on my feet. I don't think he has testified -- as a matter of fact, I think he says he has no recollection of seeing soldiers specifically burning houses in Kistanje on that day so it now assumes something that he hasn't said.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm referring to some soldiers were checking the house but some were also looting and burning some houses in paragraph 13 of --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He has now clarified and he's testified live in a manner that he doesn't recall it, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He didn't recall setting a house on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He said he didn't recall seeing a soldier setting a house on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And the question now assumes that he'd said he saw. It says, "Now, you said you saw soldiers checking houses --"

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I withdraw the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you rephrase -- yes. Our transcriber, is for very good reasons complaining for everyone talking at the same time. Apologies on behalf of all of us. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindartne. At the same time I look at the clock and then you need some time to rephrase the question. You could also take more than the two minutes remaining and take until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think we obviously overestimated my ability to go through with the questions within --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How much time do you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. President, about 20 minutes tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 20 minutes tomorrow. That's fair, in view of your earlier assessment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just one thing. I think the map 4918 was not tendered in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit P197.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And P197 is admitted into evidence. Witness, we'll resume tomorrow, although in a different courtroom, Mr. Gojanovic, and the usher will now escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to make two brief observations in view of the repeated objections against the question. I start with the last one. Did you know whether there were any civilians around, the answer is no. The next question, have you seen any civilians. Of course, the problem with these kind of questions is what is a civilian. Even if you do not know whether any civilians around, it could be that you have seen persons in civilian attire and therefore, I think intervention, the objection took more time and I don't think, as a matter of fact, a lot was lost and there was a fair chance that -- but perhaps you could have asked the question also in a different way, Ms. Mahindartne, did you see anyone in civilian clothing, because there, of course, the ambiguity who is a civilian, is that a person in civilian clothing, or what makes you believe that someone is a civilian. So, therefore, I think that the objection was certainly not necessary. Then the other matter about monocausal matters. Both when Mr. Leslie testified and Witness 54 testified I expressed the problems I had with monocausal explanations, mainly in cross-examination where the questions were put in a very monocausal way. Today something else happened. There was a very open question, that is, why did it happen. Then an explanation came. And then later on there was another explanation which at least suggested that it was not very much fit for the earlier category of persons which clearly included civilians, but, as a matter of fact disguised soldiers, whereas the second explanation given appeared to be perhaps -- to relate to a different category, and I sought clarification of this. The first question was a simple why question and was certainly not phrased in a monocausal way. This is open exchange of what I think sometimes about objections and how I phrase my questions and why I expressed my concerns in relation to Witness Leslie and to Witness 54, where I had a fear that putting the question in that way would create more or less an exclusion, of course not literally, but at least would focus the attention of the witness so much on that one single explanation that it might be difficult for the witness to think about other reasons as well or at least to focus on that, and that is what at least yesterday appeared not to be a good instrument to get the fullest information possible. No hard feelings about it. It's just I want you to let -- I want to let you know at least sometimes what is on my mind. I hope it helps you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It does, Your Honour. Let me state for the record, I won't get into it now, it will come up in cross-examination, but the Court will note that we have not raised many objections throughout the course of this trial thus far, and this is a specific reason with respect to this witness why I'm insisting on precision with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Insist on precision, I can't blame anyone for that. We adjourn until tomorrow, and the Defence might be enlightened to learn that we will not, tomorrow, Friday, the 16th of May, start at 9.00 in Courtroom II but in Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 16th day of May, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
